paragraphs.en: Progressives often support diversity mandates as a path to equality and a way to level the playing field. But all too often such policies are an insincere form of virtue-signaling that benefits only the most privileged and does little to help average people.
paragraphs.zh: 进步派人士常常支持强制推行多元化的规定，认为这是实现平等、创造公平竞争环境的途径。然而，这类政策往往只是一种缺乏诚意的美德宣示，只使最有特权的人受益，对普通人却帮助甚微。

paragraphs.en: A pair of bills sponsored by Massachusetts state Senator Jason Lewis and House Speaker Pro Tempore Patricia Haddad, to ensure “gender parity” on boards and commissions, provide a case in point.
paragraphs.zh: 马萨诸塞州参议员贾森·刘易斯与州众议院临时议长帕特里夏·哈达德发起的两项法案便是一个例子。这两项法案旨在确保各理事会及委员会实现“性别均衡”。

paragraphs.en: Haddad and Lewis are concerned that more than half the state-government boards are less than 40 percent female. In order to ensure that elite women have more such opportunities, they have proposed imposing government quotas. If the bills become law, state boards and commissions will be required to set aside 50 percent of board seats for women by 2022.
paragraphs.zh: 哈达德和刘易斯担忧的是，该州超过一半的政府理事会中，女性所占比例不足40%。为了确保精英女性获得更多此类机会，他们提议由政府强制规定配额。如果法案成为法律，到2022年，州政府各理事会及委员会就必须将50%的席位留给女性。

paragraphs.en: The bills are similar to a measure recently adopted in Califomia, which last year became the first state to require gender quotas for private companies. In signing the measure, California Governor Jerry Brown admitted that the law, which expressly classifies people on the basis of sex, is probably unconstitutional.
paragraphs.zh: 这两项法案与加利福尼亚州最近通过的一项措施相似。加州去年成为第一个要求私营企业实行性别配额的州。在签署该措施时，加州州长杰里·布朗承认，这部法律明确按照性别对人进行分类，很可能违反宪法。

paragraphs.en: The US Supreme Court frowns on sex-based classifications unless they are designed to address an “important” policy interest, Because the California law applies to all boards, even where there is no history of prior discrimination, courts are likely to rule that the law violates the constitutional guarantee of “equal protection”.
paragraphs.zh: 美国最高法院不赞同按性别分类，除非这种分类旨在服务于某项“重要”的政策利益。由于加州这项法律适用于所有董事会，甚至包括过去没有歧视历史的董事会，法院很可能裁定该法违反了宪法对“平等保护”的保障。

paragraphs.en: But are such government mandates even necessary? Female participation on corporate boards may not currently mirror the percentage of women in the general population, but so what?
paragraphs.zh: 但政府真的有必要实施此类强制规定吗？目前，公司董事会中的女性比例也许并不等同于女性在总人口中的比例，但那又怎样呢？

paragraphs.en: The number of women on corporate boards has been steadily increasing without government interference. According to a study by Catalyst, between 2010 and 2015 the share of women on the boards of global corporations increased by 54 percent.
paragraphs.zh: 在没有政府干预的情况下，公司董事会中的女性人数一直在稳步增加。根据卡塔利斯特机构的一项研究，2010年至2015年间，全球企业董事会中的女性占比提高了54%。

paragraphs.en: Requiring companies to make gender the primary qualification for board membership will inevitably lead to less experienced private sector boards. That is exactly what happened when Norway adopted a nationwide corporate gender quota.
paragraphs.zh: 要求企业把性别作为董事任职资格的首要条件，势必会降低私营企业董事会的经验水平。挪威在全国企业中实行性别配额后，出现的恰恰就是这种情况。

paragraphs.en: Writing in The New Republic, Alice Lee notes that increasing the number of opportunities for board membership without increasing the pool of qualified women to serve on such boards has led to a “golden skirt” phenomenon, where the same elite women scoop up multiple seats on a variety of boards.
paragraphs.zh: 艾丽斯·李在《新共和》杂志撰文指出，如果只增加担任董事的机会，却不扩大具备相应资格的女性人才储备，就会出现“金裙子”现象：同一批精英女性将多家董事会的多个席位揽入囊中。

paragraphs.en: Next time somebody pushes corporate quotas as a way to promote gender equity, remember that such policies are largely self-serving measures that make their sponsors feelgood but do little to help average women.
paragraphs.zh: 下次再有人把企业配额制度作为促进性别平等的办法来推销时，请记住，这类政策在很大程度上是自利的措施，让倡议者自我感觉良好，却对普通女性几乎没有帮助。
